 Most recent Most popular Bogle wants Leeds to take 'next step' published at 12:07 GMT 12:07 GMT 
 Leeds v Tottenham (12:30 GMT) 
 Leeds United full-back Jayden Bogle said the Whites cannot take their Premier League status for "granted" as the season progresses.
 It has been a stop-start 2026-27 campaign so far for Daniel Farke's side as Leeds sit 12th in the top flight.
 However, Bogle believes the west Yorkshire club belongs in the Premier League.
 "You ask any player in the squad, they will tell you Leeds belong in the Premier League," said Bogle.
 "But because of that, we can't take that for granted and sort of expect to stay here.
 "It is still the second season [in the Premier League], so we still have a massive challenge on our hands."

 Tottenham carrying all the momentum published at 12:00 GMT 12:00 GMT 
 Leeds v Tottenham (12:30 GMT) 
 Paul Birch 
BBC Sport 
 While Leeds' form has stalled, the same cannot be said for resurgent Tottenham. Without so much as a goal after four matches of the season or a win after six, three victories on the spin have propelled them from the bottom of the table and above the likes of Leeds into ninth.
 Looking far more like a Roberto de Zerbi side, they were utterly dominant against 10-man Crystal Palace last weekend. The 79.4% possession they enjoyed was their second highest in a top-flight match since records began in 2003-04.
 Up against the worst defence in the league, their much-maligned attack had a whopping 34 shots, which may have been their most in a top-flight game for a decade but the fact that only two of them went in again shined a light on their lack of clinical edge. They have the lowest xG per shot of any side this term of 0.08.
 But they certainly seem to be benefiting from having a more settled side. De Zerbi made 24 changes to his starting XI across their first seven games of this season but has made just three since they picked up their first league win of the season against Coventry .

 Leeds' mixed form published at 11:52 GMT 11:52 GMT 
 Leeds v Tottenham (12:30 GMT) 
 Paul Birch 
BBC Sport 
 How best to judge Leeds' season so far? A glass-half-empty view of only two league wins from nine games and only nine goals scored…or a positive spin on just two defeats from nine matches and a mere eight goals conceded?
 Either way, momentum for Daniel Farke's side has definitely slowed of late and their last league victory came almost two months ago when they demolished Newcastle . 
 Since that 4-1 win on 14 September they have scored the joint fewest goals (two), have the second lowest xG - both overall (4.96) and in open play (2.61) -, plus the worst final third passing accuracy (58.4%) of any top-flight side.
 How to unlock the goalscoring potential of their side remains an ongoing mission with the likes of Brenden Aaronson, Lukas Nmecha and Harry Wilson yet to find the back of the net. Their win over Newcastle is the only league game they have scored two or more goals in, and only Dominic Calvert-Lewin has netted more than once.
 But losing just three of their past 18 league games is a superb achievement and Farke's side will look to continue their impressive streak of not having lost consecutive league games since February and March last season.

 I left Man City for my mental wellbeing - Trafford published at 11:47 GMT 11:47 GMT 
 Leeds v Tottenham (12:30 GMT) 
 Keifer MacDonald 
BBC Sport 
 Media caption, Leeds United's James Trafford on his struggles at Manchester City.
 James Trafford says not playing for Manchester City last season was "horrendous" before he moved to Leeds United in the summer in search of first-team football.
 City re-signed academy graduate Trafford in July 2025, two years after he had left the club to join Championship side Burnley.
 But less than six weeks after his arrival, Italy international Gianluigi Donnarumma arrived from Paris St-Germain.
 Speaking on Football Daily's The Football Interview, Trafford reflected on the difficulties he encountered during a season on the fringes of Pep Guardiola's squad.
 "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing," said Trafford.
 "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up.
 "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing.
 "Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous."

 De Zerbi welcomes title bid ambitions published at 11:39 GMT 11:39 GMT 
 Leeds v Tottenham (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi is delighted by chief executive Vinai Venkatesham claim earlier this week that the club’s ultimate goal is to win the Premier League. 
 Spurs have finished 17th in each of the last two seasons but had a big reset in the summer with 10 new players arriving.
 “It was great to hear what Vinai said," De Zerbi said. "I think the first thing for the people to stay in this club, to work in this club is to be ambitious, but to be ambitious you have to show. 
 “And you have to show the right mentality every day, game by game because just with the words is not enough. 
 “What Vinai, the Lewis family, Johan Lange, what they are doing is something special because in the last two seasons, I think you can see they are changing a lot of things in this club. 
 “And for me as a coach, for my staff, for the players, we have to show to the (best) self to stay in this club. With the right behaviour, with the right mentality, to be hungry every day and to make a result. This is the best thing to do from our side.”

 'This will be a tight game' published at 11:23 GMT 11:23 GMT 
 Leeds v Tottenham (12:30 GMT) 
 Tottenham always seem to do well against Leeds United - they have only lost one of their past 15 meetings in the Premier League, going back almost 25 years.
 I am a little bit of a believer that some teams always do well, or badly, against certain opposition or on certain grounds.
 I had the same as a player when I had bogey teams or stadiums, as well as lucky ones. For example, while I always used to score against Everton at Goodison Park, I always had a stinker at Highfield Road, Coventry 's old home, despite getting plenty of goals against them in home games for Blackburn .
 So, I am definitely not going for Leeds to win this - but do I back Tottenham to win again and continue their good run?
 Roberto de Zerbi's side have rocketed up the table on the back of three wins in a row, although they were helped out a lot by Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card in their victory over Crystal Palace last time out.
 Tottenham are flying at the moment, and their confidence is up - we are seeing a bit of a Spurs swagger for the first time in a long while. So, while I don't think they will make it four wins in a row, I don't see them being beaten, either.
 It's likely to be a very tight game. Leeds were a bit unlucky to lose to Bournemouth last week, but their lack of goals is becoming an issue.
 Sutton's prediction: 1-1
